title: Sub-mode for orchestrator
body:
1. For example, right now our orchestrator already has two modes? (but we intelligent it figure out given the route)
    - Meta orchestrator mode: by default can be used to breakdown the task and then sequentially implement the tasks
    - Task level orchestrator: it will create an issue, implement it, and then make an PR, etc. 
2. A more general design is to have the orchestrator take an optional argument and it can load the other modes of orchestration
    - For example, best-of-n sampling, saying that the agents can implement different variants in parallel and there will be a final best aggregator choosing one based on each of the variant 
    - There could be one similar to the idea autoresearch (refer to #223 ) that supports iterative refinement 
    - Perhaps also looping 

@sepo-agent /answer what do you think?

nodes.body:
I agree with the direction. I would frame this as **orchestration strategy**, not as another value of the existing `AGENT_AUTOMATION_MODE`.

Today `AGENT_AUTOMATION_MODE` means “who decides the next handoff”: `heuristics` vs `agent` ([docs](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L5-L12), [code](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L3-L7)). The “meta orchestrator vs task-level orchestrator” distinction is currently inferred by planner output: `delegate_issue` for child/meta work, or `handoff -> implement/review/fix-pr` for normal task work ([prompt](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L30-L40), [runtime validation](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L496-L577)).

So I would add a separate optional field, something like:

```text
/orchestrate --strategy sequential
/orchestrate --strategy meta-sequential
/orchestrate --strategy best-of-n --n 4
/orchestrate --strategy research-loop
```

Internally this should probably become a typed `orchestration_strategy` input to `agent-orchestrator.yml`, not just prompt text. The workflow already has the right envelope shape for adding this kind of input ([workflow inputs](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml#L5-L72)), and handoffs already preserve structured context like `source_handoff_context`, `base_branch`, and `base_pr` ([dispatch envelope](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/cli/dispatch-agent-orchestrator.ts#L59-L78)).

The design I would use:

- Keep `AGENT_AUTOMATION_MODE = heuristics | agent` as the planner backend.
- Add `orchestration_strategy = sequential | meta-sequential | best-of-n | research-loop | loop`.
- Each strategy defines:
  - allowed planner decisions;
  - state schema;
  - resume/reducer behavior;
  - concurrency limits;
  - budget/stop rules;
  - how child work is represented in GitHub.

For example:

- `sequential`: current default bounded `implement -> review -> fix-pr -> review`.
- `meta-sequential`: current `delegate_issue` child issue model, with optional stacking via `base_pr` ([docs](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L86-L107)).
- `best-of-n`: create N independent child issues/branches, run them in parallel, then a deterministic aggregator/reviewer picks one candidate to promote.
- `research-loop`: use the experiment object from #223: run trial, parse metric, update ledger, replan next trial.
- `loop`: a generic bounded recurrence over a strategy-specific state object.

The important part: **parallel and iterative strategies need reducers, not just more planner freedom**. `best-of-n` needs a deterministic “variant result -> winner” reducer. `research-loop` needs deterministic metric parsing and best-score comparison. The LLM can propose next variants, but code should own winner selection, budget exhaustion, dedupe, and state transitions.

Implementation plan I would recommend:

1. Add `orchestration_strategy` parsing to the router/orchestrator workflow inputs.
2. Add a small strategy registry, initially mapping `sequential` to today’s behavior.
3. Move the current planner contract behind the default `sequential` strategy.
4. Add `meta-sequential` as an explicit alias for today’s `delegate_issue` behavior.
5. Add state markers for strategy metadata so resumes know which strategy they are continuing.
6. Implement `best-of-n` next, because it mostly extends existing child issue/sub-orchestrator machinery.
7. Implement `research-loop` after the experiment state/runner work from #223 exists.

I would not start by making the orchestrator prompt “smarter” and asking it to infer all of this from prose. The runtime already validates planner output against a small policy surface ([handoff validation](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L603-L615)); strategy selection should extend that policy surface explicitly.

My suggested first PR would be: **add `orchestration_strategy` with `sequential` as the default and `meta-sequential` as an explicit alias/documented mode, without changing behavior yet**. That gives us the stable API before adding `best-of-n` or `research-loop`.
